rows.text: The zeroth law makes temperature comparison possible: systems in equilibrium with the same thermometer are in equilibrium with each other.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Thermal equilibrium: no net heat transfer on contact.
Zeroth law: A↔C and B↔C in equilibrium implies A↔B in equilibrium.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Thermal Equilibrium Definition:** Two systems are in thermal equilibrium if no net heat flows between them when brought into thermal contact. This means they have the *same temperature*. Thermal equilibrium is a transitive, symmetric, and reflexive relation.  ·  **Zeroth Law Statement:** If system A is in thermal equilibrium with system B, and B is in thermal equilibrium with system C, then A is in thermal equilibrium with C. This transitive property allows temperature to be defined as a state variable that can be measured with a thermometer.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Heat is energy in transfer, not a stored substance in an equilibrium body.  ·  Equal temperatures do not imply equal masses or internal energies.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Two objects read 25°C on the same equilibrated thermometer; their temperatures match even if their masses differ.  ·  A stable thermometer reading indicates that thermometer and body have reached equilibrium.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A symbol is not a number until the unit is named.  ·  A proportional relation is not an equality until the constant is included.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: State the zeroth law and identify the thermometer’s role.  ·  Can equal-temperature objects have different internal energies? Explain.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Why wait for a thermometer reading to stabilise?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: The zeroth law says that thermal equilibrium is a transitive relation, which is why a thermometer works. The thermometer reaches equilibrium with the body, and two bodies that each match the thermometer match each other. Heat then has no tendency to flow between them.  ·  The working relations are If A is in equilibrium with C and B is in equilibrium with C, then A is in equilibrium with B and Temperature is the label of that equilibrium. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Two systems are in thermal equilibrium when no net heat flows between them after thermal contact. In ordinary conditions they then have equal temperature, but not necessarily equal internal energy: mass and material also matter.  ·  The zeroth law states that if A is in thermal equilibrium with C and B is in equilibrium with C, then A and B are in equilibrium with each other. This transitive property allows temperature to be measured consistently.  ·  A thermometer is system C. Allow it to reach a stable reading on body A, then place the same calibrated thermometer on B. Equal stable readings imply A and B have equal temperatures.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Worked case  ·  **Thermometer as 'System B':** The Zeroth law justifies using a thermometer: the thermometer (B) reaches equilibrium with the system (A), and if two systems give the same reading on the same thermometer, they are in equilibrium with each other.  ·  A vector answer needs a direction as well as a magnitude.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A special case, such as a right angle or a steady temperature, has to be stated before it is used.  ·  Body A and a thermometer both read a steady 37°C, and body B also steadies the same thermometer at 37°C. What follows for A and B?  ·  Example: a thermometer initially at 20°C placed in warm water gains energy until it and the water reach a common temperature. The final temperature need not equal either initial temperature.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Temperature predicts the direction of spontaneous heat transfer: energy flows from higher temperature to lower temperature until equilibrium, unless work or another process intervenes.  ·  **Zeroth law — applications classified** | Application | Logic | Instrument | |---|---|---| | Thermometry | Thermometer equilibrates with body | Reads common temperature | | Calibration | Fixed points define scales | Ice and steam points |
